narrative.overview:
The page is a working school lab notebook that a group has been filling in. Cool grid paper runs edge to edge behind everything, a red margin line stands to the left, and every piece of content is either printed on the journal's form, written into it by hand, or physically stuck onto it. Nothing floats in abstract space: a card is a sheet of paper, a photo is a print with tape on it, a hidden answer is a sticky note.

Print and handwriting are the system's two voices. Heavy black-ink grotesque carries the facts and the structure; blue ballpoint carries the reaction to them. Density stays comfortable and hand-made, with sheets laid slightly crooked and overlapping at the edges, so the page reads as used rather than designed. One dark block, the entry pass, is the only departure from paper.

The world refuses the dark neon space-science page and the generic kids'-club card grid.
keyCharacteristics: Cool white grid paper (24px cell) with a fixed red margin line
Heavy Onest headings set against blue Caveat handwriting
White square-cornered sheets, slightly rotated, lifted by soft navy-tinted shadows
Lime marker highlights behind single phrases, and one yellow tape
Pastel sticky notes that peel away to reveal content
One dark entry-pass block with a dashed inner border

rules.name: The Ballpoint Rule
rules.body: Handwriting on paper is blue. The only exceptions are Correction Pink for roster marks, each note's own ink, Black Ink inside the speech bubble, and lime on the dark block.

rules.name: The One Stroke Rule
rules.body: A heading or handwritten conclusion carries at most one lime-highlighted phrase, and the text over it keeps its own ink: Black Ink in headings, Ballpoint Blue in conclusions. Lime is never text on paper.

rules.name: The One Pink Rule
rules.body: Outside the sticky notes, pink has one value, dark enough to read as text. Correction Pink both draws and writes.

rules.name: The One Dark Page Rule
rules.body: A page gets one dark block, the entry pass. Everything else stays on paper.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Print states; handwriting responds. Headings, explanations, and form labels are Onest. Answers, conclusions, captions, and filled-in values are Caveat, and never run past a sentence or two.

rules.name: The Form Field Rule
rules.body: A small tracked label names a field whose value sits directly beside or beneath it, as on a printed form. It never introduces a heading.

rules.name: The Reading Tilt Rule
rules.body: The more text a sheet holds, the less it tilts: small photo prints up to 3deg, the hero photo 2.5deg, the portrait sheet 1.5deg, the roster 1deg, protocol sheets about 0.4deg in alternating directions. The entry pass does not tilt.

rules.name: The Square Paper Rule
rules.body: If it is paper, its corners are square.

rules.name: The Framed Пушистик Rule
rules.body: The artwork keeps its original grey background, because a clean cutout was not achievable. Show it only inside a frame, as a round sticker with a white border.

dos: Do lay new content on paper as a physical object: a sheet, a print, a note, or a line written directly on the grid.
Do write handwriting in Ballpoint Blue (#1f3fc4), and use Correction Pink (#cc1f62) for any pink text on white.
Do give each sticky note its paired inks, in the yellow, pink, green order.
Do tilt sheets by how much text they hold, from about 0.4deg for protocols up to 3deg for small prints.
Do show Пушистик only as a round sticker with a white border.
Do tint soft shadows on paper navy (rgba(20,30,80,…)) and keep them wide.
Do keep the 3px dashed focus outline, lime on the dark block, and the reduced-motion fallbacks on anything new.
donts: Don't cut Пушистик out of its grey background or place the artwork unframed on the grid.
Don't add a second pink outside the sticky notes, or use lime for text on paper.
Don't add a second dark block to a page.
Don't reuse the dashed portrait slot as a pattern; replace it with the real photo.
Don't round the corners of paper.
Don't put more than one lime highlight in a heading or conclusion.
Don't drift toward a dark neon space-science page or a generic kids'-club card grid.
